text: what does error QRV-4012 mean
design_note: Exact rare token (error code). Embeddings treat QRV-4012 as noise; BM25 should nail it. The index page lists the code with a one-liner: partial credit, and a lexical near-trap above the real entry.

text: flush_interval_ms default
design_note: Exact parameter name with no natural-language context. Vector search has almost nothing to embed; the API reference is the only doc naming it.

text: checkpoint_store_uri setting
design_note: Exact config key. The yaml reference defines it (2); the checkpointing guide mentions it in passing (1).

text: my pipeline produces data faster than the database can accept and memory keeps growing
design_note: Describes backpressure without using 'backpressure', 'flow', 'buffer', or 'stage'. BM25 has nothing rare to grip; the embedding must carry it.

text: guarantee each record is applied a single time even if the runner crashes mid-way
design_note: Paraphrase of effectively-once delivery; shares almost no tokens with the target's own terms. Checkpointing explains the recovery mechanism but not the guarantee: partial.

text: where do records end up when they fail over and over
design_note: Paraphrase of dead-letter routing avoiding 'dead', 'letter', 'queue', 'retry'. The retry guide mentions the hand-off once: partial.

text: set up OAuth authentication for a pipeline
design_note: The changelog says 'OAuth' seven times and answers nothing; the guide says it twice and answers everything. Token-frequency ranking takes the bait.

text: configure retry behavior for transient failures
design_note: The API index is dense with retry-named symbols and explains none of them. BM25 favors it; the guide is the answer.

text: enable schema validation on a source
design_note: The FAQ repeats the phrase 'schema validation' in five question titles and answers none of them. The guide answers in its first sentence.

text: authenticate a connector with an API key
design_note: OAuth guide is the semantic sibling (both 'authentication'); embeddings pull it in, but it does not answer the API-key question. Graded 0 by design.

text: increase pipeline throughput by tuning batch size
design_note: Rate-limits is the sibling: semantically 'about limits on speed' but it concerns the REST endpoint cap, not batch tuning. Graded 0.

text: write pipeline output to an S3 bucket
design_note: Directional confusion: source vs sink for the same backend. Embeddings see near-identical text; only the direction differs. Source graded 0.

text: how do I start a pipeline in Quorva v1
design_note: Version-pinned ask. The v2 page is right topic, wrong version (1); migration shows both (1). Retrievers that ignore the version token rank v2 first.

text: qv.execute() arguments in v2
design_note: Pinned to v2 by symbol and by word. The v1 page documents a different API entirely: graded 0. Migration maps the arguments: partial.

text: migrate run() calls from v1 to v2
design_note: The migration page is the only one that maps old names to new. Each version's own page covers one side: partial each.

text: configure the DLQ
design_note: The dead-letter guide never uses the acronym; only the glossary bridges DLQ to dead-letter queue. Lexical match fails; embeddings may or may not bridge it.

text: does Quorva support exactly-once processing
design_note: The docs' term is 'effectively-once'; the community's is 'exactly-once'. Zero lexical overlap on the term that matters.

text: what is the QPS limit on the ingest API
design_note: Docs say 'requests per second'; the query says QPS. The glossary defines the acronym: partial credit and the only lexical bridge.

text: run a pipeline without checkpointing
design_note: 'Without X' where the X guide is the strongest match on both signals. The checkpointing guide names the key but not how to turn it off: partial.

text: authenticate without storing secrets in the config file
design_note: Both auth guides show config-file credentials and match 'authenticate' strongly; both graded 0. Only the environment/workload-identity page satisfies the constraint.

text: deploy a pipeline without using the CLI
design_note: The CLI deploy page is the lexical and semantic magnet for 'deploy'; the constraint excludes it. Graded 0 by design.

text: QRV-5002 checkpoint corrupt
design_note: Exact error code with no natural-language context; embeddings treat QRV-5002 as noise. The index page lists it with a one-liner (partial); the dedicated page answers it.

text: batch_rows argument on PostgresSink
design_note: Exact parameter + symbol name. Only the API reference names batch_rows; nothing to embed semantically.

text: commit_interval_s default
design_note: Exact config key whose default (30) is stated in the checkpointing guide (2); the yaml reference lists the key (1).

text: qv.execute limit argument
design_note: Exact v2 symbol + argument. The v2 page is the only doc naming qv.execute's limit; v1 uses max_records, so it must not win.

text: dead_letter_uri key
design_note: Exact config key; the DLQ guide defines it (2), the yaml reference lists it (1).

text: will records come out in the same sequence they went in
design_note: Paraphrase of ordering guarantees; avoids 'order', 'partition', 'sequence'-as-noun. Minimal lexical overlap with the target.

text: avoid reprocessing everything from the start after a crash
design_note: Describes checkpoint resume without 'checkpoint', 'offset', 'resume'. Delivery guide covers the recovery it enables (partial).

text: spread one slow step across more cpu cores
design_note: Paraphrase of parallelism/workers avoiding those words. Performance page touches scaling (partial).

text: stop one slow stage from eating all the memory
design_note: Second backpressure angle, different wording from q-par-1; still avoids 'backpressure'/'buffer'.

text: make applying the same write twice harmless
design_note: Paraphrase of idempotency avoiding the word. Delivery guide leans on it (partial).

text: change the batch size to improve Postgres write throughput
design_note: qrv-tuning-faq covers 'batch size', 'Postgres', 'write throughput', 'improve' across unanswered questions; the API reference answers using 'batch_rows'/'flush' and fewer query words. Distinct-term coverage should rank the FAQ first on BM25.

text: retry a failed webhook delivery with backoff
design_note: qrv-webhook-changelog hits retry/failed/webhook/delivery/backoff every line; the retry guide explains backoff with other words. Coverage trap.

text: validate the pipeline configuration before deploying
design_note: qrv-deploy-faq saturates validate/pipeline/configuration/deploy; qrv-cli-validate is the actual answer. Coverage trap.

text: set the commit interval for checkpoint state
design_note: qrv-config-index lists commit/interval/checkpoint/state as bare keys; the checkpointing guide answers (2), yaml reference lists the key (1).

text: authenticate the webhook sink with an API key
design_note: qrv-auth-faq repeats authenticate/webhook/sink/API/key across unanswered Qs; the api-key guide is the real answer. Coverage trap.

text: bring changes from a Postgres database into the pipeline
design_note: Near-sibling qrv-sink-postgres (writes TO postgres) is the embedding magnet and shares 'Postgres'/'sink' tokens; the query is about reading FROM. Sink graded 0 by omission; direction is the whole trap.

text: cap how many records a single run will process
design_note: Sibling qrv-guide-rate-limits ('limit' on the API) is semantically adjacent; the answer is qv.execute's limit argument. Rate-limits graded 0.

text: watch per-stage record counts and timings while it runs
design_note: Sibling qrv-cli-status (also 'while it runs', reports health) is the magnet; metrics endpoint is the answer. Status graded 0 -- it reports control-plane state, not per-stage counts.

text: sign requests with a credential that expires and refreshes
design_note: Sibling qrv-auth-apikey (keys do NOT expire) shares 'credential'/'auth' space; only OAuth (tokens expire/refresh) fits. API-key graded 0.

text: the fastest file source for columnar typed data
design_note: Siblings qrv-source-csv / qrv-source-jsonl are file sources too (embedding-close); only Parquet is columnar. Others graded 0 by omission.

text: add a sink in Quorva v1
design_note: v1-pinned. The v2 .to() page is right topic wrong version (1); migration maps them (1). Retrievers ignoring the version token rank v2 first.

text: the .to() operator for attaching sinks in v2
design_note: v2-pinned by exact operator; v1 add_sink page is a different API, graded 0. Migration maps (1).

text: blocking argument to run() in v1
design_note: v1 symbol (blocking, run()). v2 uses wait on qv.execute, so the v2 page must not win. Migration maps (1).

text: what replaced max_records in v2
design_note: Only the migration page maps old->new (max_records -> limit); each version page covers one side (partial).

text: state_uri versus state_dir
design_note: The rename is documented only on the migration page (2); v2 page names state_uri (1).

text: set up a CDC source
design_note: Docs say 'change data capture' / 'logical-replication slot', never 'CDC'. Only the extended glossary bridges the acronym (1); the Postgres source is the answer (2).

text: tail latency of sink writes
design_note: Docs say 'p99 write latency'; query says 'tail latency'. Glossary-ext defines the synonym (1); batching guide is the answer (2).

text: does it support 2PC for sink writes
design_note: Delivery guide says 'two-phase commit', never '2PC'. Glossary-ext bridges (1).

text: RPS ceiling on the ingest API
design_note: Docs say 'requests per second'; query says RPS. Both glossaries bridge (1); rate-limits answers (2).

text: at-least-once versus exactly-once delivery
design_note: Docs' term is 'effectively-once'; query uses the industry pair. Zero overlap on the decisive term.

text: run a pipeline without deploying it to a fleet
design_note: qrv-cli-deploy and qrv-deployment-overview are the lexical+semantic magnets for 'pipeline'/'fleet'; the constraint excludes them. Local run is the answer; deploy pages graded 0.

text: read a source without tracking offsets or resuming
design_note: Checkpointing/offset docs are the strong match on both signals; the constraint wants state off. Ephemeral is the answer; checkpointing names the knob (1).

text: let a bad record through without failing its batch
design_note: Schema-enforce docs match 'record'/'batch'/'fail' strongly; the constraint wants the non-failing path -- warn mode, in the schema guide.

text: run without persisting any pipeline state
design_note: Second ephemeral angle; checkpointing is the magnet, the constraint excludes it (named partial).

text: supply credentials without environment variables, from a file
design_note: qrv-auth-env (environment credentials) is the magnet and the excluded path; the file-based api-key guide satisfies the constraint (2). Env page named partial because it's the contrast, not graded 0, to keep the trap honest.

text: what checkpoint interval does each Quorva runner use by default
design_note: Support set: the three runner docs. Each names its interval in a different sentence, so a single retrieved chunk cannot answer it; set recall and full support measure how much of the set is surfaced.

text: which runner guarantees exactly-once delivery and which only at-least-once
design_note: Support set: the three runner docs. Two are at-least-once and one is exactly-once for transactional sinks; the answer needs all three to make the comparison.

text: what is the maximum number of in-flight batches for each runner
design_note: Support set: the three runner docs, each with a distinct in-flight cap (8, 64 per worker, 4). Lexical overlap is high, so retrieval must return all three, not the best-matching one.

text: what memory ceiling does each runner enforce
design_note: Support set: the three runner docs (512 MiB, 2 GiB per worker, 256 MiB). Units differ, so the answer is only complete with every member.

text: what is the p95 latency SLA for each region
design_note: Support set: the four region docs, each stating its own p95 SLA (120/80/180/150 ms). Four-way aggregation; missing any region is an incomplete answer.

text: how long does each region retain stored records by default
design_note: Support set: the four region docs. Two retain 30 days and two 45 days; the grouping is only visible with the whole set.

text: which regions require in-region data residency
design_note: Support set: the four region docs; every region pins data in-region, so the correct answer is the full set and a partial retrieval under-answers.

text: what are the regional edge endpoints
design_note: Support set: the four region docs, each naming one quorva-edge-* endpoint. The identifiers are lexically similar, which stresses returning all four rather than the closest match.

text: what access token lifetime applies to each authentication method
design_note: Support set: the three auth docs (15 minutes, 1 hour, 10 minutes). Each lifetime appears once; the answer needs all three.

text: which authentication methods rotate credentials automatically
design_note: Support set: the three auth docs. The answer distinguishes schedules: mTLS rotates certificates every 24 hours, workload identity on restart, OIDC via refresh token.

text: what audit identifier is recorded for each authentication method
design_note: Support set: the three auth docs (peer_serial, spiffe_id, sub). Three exact tokens spread across three documents.

text: which authentication methods does Quorva support for service access
design_note: Support set: the three auth docs. This is the membership query of the auth group; a single-document answer names only one method.

text: what delivery guarantee does each streaming sink provide
design_note: Support set: the three sink docs. All are at-least-once, with Pub/Sub offering exactly-once only via subscription configuration; completeness is the point.

text: what maximum message size does each streaming sink accept
design_note: Support set: the three sink docs (1 MiB, 1 MiB, 10 MiB). Two values repeat, so a partial answer can look right by accident; full support is the discriminating metric.

text: how is ordering preserved in each streaming sink
design_note: Support set: the three sink docs (per partition, per shard, ordering key). The wording differs per doc, so embeddings see three different phrasings.

text: how long does each streaming sink retain messages by default
design_note: Support set: the three sink docs. Kafka defers retention to the broker; Kinesis 24 hours; Pub/Sub 7 days. One member has no sink-side default, which only a full retrieval reveals.

text: why did fleet pipelines stall in February 2026
design_note: Joining entity: RunnerLease, named in both the fleet-runner doc and the February postmortem. Neither document alone explains the stall: one defines the lease, the other records the race.

text: what role does RunnerLease play in fleet checkpointing
design_note: Joining entity: RunnerLease. The fleet doc states the renewal period; the postmortem states what a stale renewal causes. The join is the entity, not shared wording.

text: what caused the May 2026 EU outage and which endpoint was involved
design_note: Joining entity: quorva-edge-eu, the endpoint the region doc defines and the postmortem blames. Required documents: qrv-region-eu and qrv-incident-2026-05-eu.

text: what is the eu-west-1 latency SLA and how did its edge endpoint fail
design_note: Joining entity: quorva-edge-eu. The SLA lives in the region doc; the failure lives in the postmortem; both are required to answer.

text: what should I do about the CertificateAuthority intermediate rotation
design_note: Joining entity: CertificateAuthority, named in the mTLS doc and the advisory. The action follows only when both are read: what the CA is and what the rotation requires.

text: how long do mTLS client certificates last and what changed in the CA rotation advisory
design_note: Joining entity: CertificateAuthority. Certificate lifetime is in the auth doc; the trust-bundle change is in the advisory. Neither alone answers the question.

text: why did Kafka sink duplicates increase after a consumer rebalance
design_note: Joining entity: KafkaPublisher. The sink doc defines at-least-once; the postmortem explains why a retry became visible downstream.

text: which sink uses KafkaPublisher and what delivery guarantee does it promise
design_note: Joining entity: KafkaPublisher. The July postmortem names the publisher in a rebalance context; the sink doc supplies the guarantee.

text: does quorva replay write checkpoints
design_note: Joining entity: EphemeralMode, defined in the runner doc and applied to replay in the CLI doc. The answer is a join: replay's behaviour is inherited from the mode.

text: how does EphemeralMode affect replay and what is its memory ceiling
design_note: Joining entity: EphemeralMode. The ceiling is in the runner doc, the replay consequence in the CLI doc.

text: what caused the APAC latency breach in September 2026
design_note: Joining entity: quorva-edge-ap. The region doc supplies the SLA and the endpoint; the postmortem supplies the failover cause.

text: what is the ap-southeast-2 p95 SLA and how did its endpoint miss it
design_note: Joining entity: quorva-edge-ap. SLA in the region doc; measured breach in the postmortem.

text: why did OIDC logins fail in October 2026
design_note: Joining entity: OidcBroker. The auth doc defines the broker; the postmortem records its refresh rejection.

text: what token lifetime does OidcBroker issue and what caused the refresh failures
design_note: Joining entity: OidcBroker. Token lifetime is in the auth doc; the clock-skew cause in the postmortem. The postmortem explicitly rules out lifetime as the cause.

text: how does the embedded scheduler treat slow transforms
design_note: Joining entity: EmbeddedScheduler, defined in the runner doc and tuned in the tuning doc. Fairness behaviour needs both.

text: what is the default checkpoint interval for the embedded runner and how is fairness tuned
design_note: Joining entity: EmbeddedScheduler. The default interval is in the runner doc; the scheduling interaction is in the tuning doc.
